what_is_jeevan_umang.content: Jeevan Umang is a participating whole-life plan that provides an ongoing (lifelong) survival income after the premium paying term. It combines life insurance protection with a recurring income stream — making it attractive for retirement planning. The plan also accrues bonuses and may include final additional bonuses where applicable.

how_it_works.h2: How the LIC Jeevan Umang calculator works (formulas explained)
how_it_works.content_premium:
• Base annual premium = lookup from LIC rate table depending on Age, BSA and PPT.
  • Mode conversion (to monthly/quarterly/half-yearly) uses modal loading factors:
    • Yearly × 1.00 = Yearly
    • Half-yearly = Yearly × 0.5098
    • Quarterly = Yearly × 0.2575
    • Monthly = Yearly × 0.0879

(Your calculator should compute and display all four modes when you enter a yearly premium.)
how_it_works.content_ga:
• GAs are paid during the Premium Paying Term at a fixed rate per ₹1,000 of BSA (displayed by the plan).
  • Total GAs = Annual GA × PPT.
how_it_works.content_income:
• Regular income is typically expressed as a percentage of BSA paid annually after PPT (e.g., many LIC whole-life income plans pay ~8% of BSA as yearly income; verify current brochure rate).
  • Flexi / accumulate options: if offered, unwithdrawn income may accumulate at a guaranteed rate.
how_it_works.content_maturity:
• For whole-life income plans, the main benefit is the lifetime income; death benefit typically equals Sum Assured on Death (as per brochure) or guaranteed minimum (e.g., 105% of total premiums paid). Check the plan UIN for exact terms.

> Accuracy note: Where the plan uses declared bonuses or special additions, the calculator uses illustrative/default values but always shows a clear disclaimer and 'last updated' date.

inputs_explained.h2: Inputs explained (what each field means and why it matters)
inputs_explained.content_age: Younger entrants pay lower premiums; gender may affect premium in some tables (if allowed by the insurer/regulator).
inputs_explained.content_bsa: This is the core coverage amount — both survival income and Guaranteed Additions are derived from BSA.
inputs_explained.content_ppt: Shorter PPT = higher annual premium but faster income start or lower total premium years. Typical PPT options include several discrete choices (e.g., 10, 12, 15 years) — use the preset list.
inputs_explained.content_mode: Yearly is cheapest (lowest modal loading). Monthly is convenient but slightly costlier due to modal loading.
inputs_explained.content_riders: Optional covers (Accidental Death & Disability, Critical Illness) add separate premium lines and do not normally change GA or survival income but do increase the payable premium.

surrender_loan.h2: Surrender, paid-up & loans — what the calculator shows
surrender_loan.content:
• Paid-up value: If premiums stop after 2+ years, policy becomes paid-up. Paid-up SA reduces proportionately to premiums paid; calculator can simulate paid-up outcomes.
  • Surrender value: Available after the policy acquires surrender value (usually after 2 yrs). Calculator estimates Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV) based on paid premiums and vested benefits.
  • Loan: You can take a loan against the policy up to a percentage of SSV — calculator shows an estimated loan amount and interest impact.

tips.h2: Practical tips to reduce premium or improve value
tips.content:
• Pay yearly — modal loading is smallest.
  • Pick a longer PPT (if you can afford the time) — reduces annual premium.
  • Avoid unnecessary riders — only add riders you truly need.
  • Start earlier — age is the single biggest determinant of premium.
  • Check high SA rebates — if you’re going for large sums assured, you may get a discount.

faq_list.q: What is the Jeevan Umang calculator and is it free?
faq_list.a: The Jeevan Umang calculator is a free online tool to estimate premiums, survival income and related values for LIC Plan 745. It provides quick, illustrative figures — not a binding LIC quote.

faq_list.q: How do I calculate Jeevan Umang premium?
faq_list.a: Enter your age, BSA, PPT and mode into the calculator. The tool uses LIC rate tables (or illustrative assumptions) and modal factors to compute yearly and mode premiums.

faq_list.q: What is the survival income under Jeevan Umang?
faq_list.a: Survival income is a yearly payment after PPT — typically a fixed percentage of Basic Sum Assured (the specific percent is defined in the plan brochure). The calculator displays this as an annual amount.

faq_list.q: Does the calculator include riders and GST?
faq_list.a: Yes — toggle riders to see additional rider premiums. The calculator also shows GST (first year/renewal rates) in the premium breakdown.
Results are estimates. For a binding quote and acceptance, contact LIC or an authorized agent. The calculator is accurate to the extent of the input assumptions (bonus, FAB, rebate rates).

faq_list.q: Can NRIs use the Jeevan Umang calculator?
faq_list.a: Yes, NRIs can use the calculator for planning, but actual purchase and eligibility depend on LIC and FEMA rules.

faq_list.q: When can I take a loan against Jeevan Umang?
faq_list.a: Loans are typically available after the policy acquires a surrender value (commonly after 2 full years). The calculator estimates the loanable amount based on SSV.
Generally, policy payouts under life insurance may be tax-favored under Section 10(10D), but tax laws change — consult a tax advisor.
If premiums stop after at least two full years, your policy becomes paid-up. The calculator can show the reduced paid-up SA and expected maturity/paid-up benefits.

faq_list.q: How to compare Jeevan Umang with Jeevan Utsav or Jeevan Labh?
faq_list.a: Use the side-by-side comparison feature: input identical BSA and check income vs maturity outcomes to choose the best fit for your goals.
